description:
The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is a welfare initiative aimed at providing financial assistance to workers in the unorganized sector in India. 

This scheme is specifically designed for the benefit of construction workers. 

The scheme was launched by the Government of India under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996. 

The primary objective of the Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is to provide financial support to construction workers for travel expenses incurred during their leave. 

The scheme aims to improve the living standards of construction workers by facilitating their travel to their native places. 

The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is intended to cover the travel expenses of construction workers and their families. 

Eligible beneficiaries can receive financial assistance for travel expenses up to a maximum limit of INR 1,000 per worker. 

This amount is intended to cover the costs associated with travel by rail or road. 

The scheme is designed to provide assistance for one journey per year. 

The financial assistance is provided only for the journey to the native place of the worker. 

To be eligible for this scheme, the applicant must be a registered construction worker under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996. 

The applicant must also be a member of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

There are no specific age limits for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, the applicant must be actively engaged in construction work. 

The income criteria for eligibility under this scheme is that the worker's income should not exceed INR 15,000 per month. 

The application process for the Leave Travelling Concession Scheme involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must obtain the application form from the local office of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The application form can also be downloaded from the official website of the respective state welfare board. 

The applicant must fill out the form with accurate details regarding their identity and employment. 

The applicant must provide proof of their registration as a construction worker. 

This proof can be in the form of a registration certificate issued by the welfare board. 

Additionally, the applicant must submit a copy of their identity proof such as an Aadhaar card or voter ID. 

The application must also include a declaration of the worker's income. 

Once the application form is completed, it should be submitted to the local office of the welfare board. 

The application can be submitted in person or through a registered post. 

After submission, the welfare board will verify the details provided in the application. 

The verification process may take up to 30 days. 

Once the application is approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed to the worker's bank account. 

The disbursement is typically made within 15 days of approval. 

It is important for applicants to keep track of their application status. 

They can do this by contacting the local welfare board office or checking the official website. 

The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

The specific implementing authority is the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board in each state. 

Each state has its own welfare board that manages the scheme at the local level. 

For instance, the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board is responsible for implementing the scheme in Delhi. 

Contact details for the respective welfare boards can be found on the official Ministry of Labour and Employment website. 

The scheme is part of a broader effort by the Indian government to improve the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector. 

The government recognizes that construction workers often face financial hardships and lack access to basic amenities. 

By providing financial assistance for travel, the scheme aims to alleviate some of these burdens. 

The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is one of several initiatives aimed at supporting the welfare of construction workers. 

Other initiatives include health insurance schemes and educational assistance for workers' children. 

The government has allocated significant funds for the implementation of this scheme. 

In the financial year 2022-2023, the government allocated approximately INR 500 crores for the welfare of construction workers. 

The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is expected to benefit millions of construction workers across the country. 

As of October 2023, there are over 50 lakh registered construction workers in India. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the mobility of these workers, allowing them to visit their families more frequently. 

This is particularly important for workers who migrate to urban areas for employment. 

The scheme also aims to promote social inclusion by facilitating travel for workers and their families. 

The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is an essential component of the government's commitment to improving the lives of workers in the unorganized sector. 

It reflects the government's understanding of the challenges faced by construction workers. 

The scheme is designed to provide tangible benefits to workers and their families. 

Overall, the Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is a crucial welfare initiative that aims to support the travel needs of construction workers in India. 

It provides financial assistance that can significantly ease the burden of travel expenses. 

This scheme is a testament to the government's ongoing efforts to enhance the welfare of vulnerable workers in the country. 

By addressing the travel needs of construction workers, the scheme contributes to their overall well-being and quality of life. 

The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is an important step towards ensuring that construction workers receive the support they need. 

It is a vital resource for those who often work in challenging conditions and face economic hardships. 

The scheme is expected to continue evolving to meet the needs of construction workers in India. 

The government remains committed to improving the welfare of this essential workforce. 

The Leave Travelling Concession Scheme is an integral part of this commitment.
